senses.en_definition: An English preposition indicating direction, destination, or a recipient. This describes its English use only; it does not establish the sense of the frequency-list entry.

messages.en: Whose email address do I put in this “To” field? I need to send off that form.
Just put our supervisor’s email address. It’s in the message I sent you earlier.
Push the trolley a bit more slowly. I’m holding the box on top steady.
Okay, I’ll push it slowly. Have you got the box?

senses.en_definition: To help or assist someone through physical effort, money, ideas, or other support.
To rescue someone from danger; to relieve suffering or help cure an illness.

collocations.en: help people injured in an accident

senses.en_definition: Please; used before a verb to make a request or soften an instruction.

messages.en: Are you still at that stall? Could you get me a packet of nasi lemak? I haven’t eaten yet.
Still here. Want a fried egg with it?
Yes, thanks! I’ll transfer you the money in a bit.

senses.en_definition: Please; used to make an earnest request or plea for someone to do something.

collocations.en: please give me my money back

senses.en_definition: Used to plead directly for help or rescue for oneself or someone else.

collocations.en: please help me; please save me

messages.en: I’m heading out to get lunch. Have you eaten?
Not yet. Please get me a rice meal while you’re there. I can’t get away right now—still got loads of work to do.
Sure. Chicken rice as usual, right? I’ll message you when I get there.
